headline: 10 tourists killed: Cox's Bazar resort operated without approval
summary: The TUPTUP Resto and Resort in Inani was operating illegally and lacked fire safety clearance despite a prior warning from the Fire Service.
details: A devastating fire at the TUPTUP Resto and Resort in Inani, Cox's Bazar, has claimed the lives of 10 tourists.
Fire Service Director General Brig Gen Sultanul Afrain Junaid revealed that the resort was operating without the required authorization and had no fire safety clearance.
The Fire Service had inspected the resort in June and issued a formal notice warning that the facility was unsafe for guests.
Despite this official warning, the resort continued to operate illegally, leading to the tragediay.
The victims include members of a single family, with six people from one family alone being killed in the blaze.
Some guests were forced to jump from the second floor to escape the flames as the fire spread rapidly through the structure.
caption:
10 tourists killed in a resort fire. The Fire Service had warned the resort was unsafe months before the tragedy.

A devastating fire at the TUPTUP Resto and Resort in Inani, Cox's Bazar, has claimed the lives of 10 tourists.

Fire Service Director General Brig Gen Sultanul Afrain Junaid revealed that the resort was operating without the required authorization and had no fire safety clearance.

The Fire Service had inspected the resort in June and issued a formal notice warning that the facility was unsafe for guests.

Despite this official warning, the resort continued to operate illegally, leading to the tragediay.

The victims include members of a single family, with six people from one family alone being killed in the blaze.

Some guests were forced to jump from the second floor to escape the flames as the fire spread rapidly through the structure.

Source: bdnews24.com, Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo, The Daily Star

headline: Doctor suspended after PM catches him smoking in hospital room
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman ordered the immediate suspension of a doctor at Bangladesh Shishu Hospital after finding him smoking in his office during a surprise visit.
details: A doctor at Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute has been suspended after Prime Minister Tarique Rahman found him smoking in his office during a surprise inspection on Saturday.
The Prime Minister expressed strong dissatisfaction with the doctor's behavior and the untidy condition of the office room, according to Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu.
Tarique Rahman instructed Prof AKM Azizul Haque, chairman of the hospital's governing board, to take immediate disciplinary action, leading to the suspension of Dr Rafiqul Islam.
The visit was part of a day-long tour of hospitals and educational institutions across Dhaka to assess dengue prevention measures and general cleanliness.
Earlier in the day, the Prime Minister visited the Kuwait-Bangladesh Friendship Government Hospital in Uttara, where he also expressed dissatisfaction with the management.
During the tour, the the Prime Minister urged doctors and staff to maintain hygiene and carry out their duties with responsibility.
caption:
A surprise visit by the Prime Minister leads to a doctor's immediate suspension after he was caught smoking in his office.

A doctor at Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute has been suspended after Prime Minister Tarique Rahman found him smoking in his office during a surprise inspection on Saturday.

The Prime Minister expressed strong dissatisfaction with the doctor's behavior and the untidy condition of the office room, according to Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu.

Tarique Rahman instructed Prof AKM Azizul Haque, chairman of the hospital's governing board, to take immediate disciplinary action, leading to the suspension of Dr Rafiqul Islam.

The visit was part of a day-long tour of hospitals and educational institutions across Dhaka to assess dengue prevention measures and general cleanliness.

Earlier in the day, the Prime Minister visited the Kuwait-Bangladesh Friendship Government Hospital in Uttara, where he also expressed dissatisfaction with the management.

During the tour, the the Prime Minister urged doctors and staff to maintain hygiene and carry out their duties with responsibility.

#Bangladesh #Dhaka #HealthCare #Accountability #News

Source: Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV, bdnews24.com, The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune
